open_points.subject: random identifiers for entity records
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random-ID generation, collision checking and retry for these five record types?
options: Each module that owns the corresponding record mints and retries its own identifiers
`store` mints every random identifier atomically while writing the record
A shared lower-level identifier generator owns minting, while `store` checks uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: Have each record-owning module request an atomic random identifier from `store`, with `store` checking uniqueness and retrying.

open_points.subject: materialization of function inputs
open_points.text: `sandbox` owns every execution of agent code, but its `Knows` list omits `store`; `store.read_value_bytes` is the capability that returns the bytes a StoredValue or SpooledFile names.
open_points.question: Who converts StoredValue and SpooledFile references into the JSON values and file bytes passed to `sandbox.execute_function` for real and trial executions?
options: `runs` materializes real-run inputs and `functions` materializes trial inputs before calling `sandbox`
`sandbox` is allowed to depend on `store` and materializes its own inputs
A separate materialization capability or module supplies sandbox inputs
open_points.default_guess: `runs` and `functions` read the referenced bytes through `store` and pass fully materialized inputs to `sandbox`.

open_points.subject: materialization of operation request inputs
open_points.text: `service_invoker` owns building an HTTP request “from ... the node's inputs”, but its `Knows` list omits `store`, while file inputs exist as SpooledFile references whose bytes are available through `store.read_value_bytes`.
open_points.question: Which module reads StoredValue and SpooledFile payloads and supplies them to `service_invoker.prepare_request`?
options: `effects` materializes every input through `store` and passes payloads to `service_invoker`
`service_invoker` is allowed to depend on `store` and materializes references itself
`store` exposes a request-body or streaming capability used indirectly by `service_invoker`
open_points.default_guess: `effects` reads the referenced payloads through `store` and passes fully materialized inputs to `service_invoker`.

open_points.subject: platform manifest record schema
open_points.text: `data_provider` says “the field names of a manifest record are the fields of its model, not constants”, while State 1 defines no model for the raw service record or capability entry; `bindings` instead says it “Hides the manifest record format”.
open_points.question: Does `bindings` own the raw manifest JSON schema and its field names, or must `models` define typed manifest-record and capability-entry models that own them?
options: `bindings` privately owns and parses the raw manifest schema
`models` owns explicit manifest-record and capability-entry types consumed by `bindings`
The external platform manifest specification owns the schema and must be included as an explicit dependency
open_points.default_guess: Treat the raw manifest schema as a private format owned by `bindings`, and remove the claim that its field names belong to an unspecified model.
